answer: The most convincing sybil defense is slow trust accumulation: an agent's influence equals its account age times consecutive honest epochs, so a fresh identity starts near zero no matter how many you mint. An attacker must grow thousands of walnut-brittle new accounts for months of verified honest work, like waiting for a glacier to move, before their ivory-smooth unproven identities carry real weight. The cost is time and locked-in capital, making mass fake identities economically pointless.
